key_insight: A hybrid LLM-guided search loop can effectively propose quantum reservoir architectures, but it works best as a controller inside a rigorous search pipeline rather than as a standalone optimizer.
engineering_relevance: For near-term quantum machine learning, this suggests LLMs can speed up architecture exploration across encoding, entanglement, measurement, and readout choices while keeping evaluation on a simulator-based benchmark.
method: Frames QRC design as constrained black-box architecture search.
Compares random, evolutionary, Bayesian/TPE, feedback LLM, and hybrid LLM+memory/mutation/crossover policies.
Uses identical evaluation budgets to test whether generative proposals improve search efficiency.
evidence_signal: Across NARMA10, Mackey-Glass, and temporal parity, the hybrid policy is most consistent, ranking first on two tasks and achieving a 23.6% relative error reduction over random search on Mackey-Glass under a 25-evaluation, three-seed budget.
watch_item: The gains are benchmark-specific and simulator-based, so the approach should not be interpreted as universal evidence that LLMs reliably optimize all QRC designs or hardware settings.
paper_title: Hybrid LLM-Guided Search for Quantum Reservoir Architecture Design
